target_customer: Individuals and small businesses wanting a simple mobile optimized website, paying monthly subscriptions
problem: Building a good looking site that works on mobile required design and coding or two separate sites.
business_model: freemium SaaS subscription for site hosting and upgrades

founders.name: David Chen
founders.background_notes: Per the YC Q&A the founders were college students who built sites for student organizations; YC rejected their first application.

founders.name: Dafeng Guo
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and the YC Q&A.

founders.name: Teng Bao
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and the YC Q&A.

competitors.name: Squarespace
competitors.what: Design focused site builder and host

technical_complexity.rationale: Template based one page site builder; mobile responsive design was the differentiator.

defensibility.rationale: Larger rivals could copy the one page mobile approach; hosted sites add some switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals added mobile responsive features, yet Strikingly stayed independent and grew in China.

market_need_then: Mobile traffic was rising in 2012 to 2013 and rivals required separate mobile sites, per The Next Web (2013-04).

identity.voice_and_tone: aspirational, manifesto page on the site

branding.brand_signature: One click site creation and the manifesto page
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage as the first Chinese company to graduate from YC, per Wikipedia and Branding Magazine.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized among site builders and described positively in press, but not iconic.

pivots.to: landing page builder that became Strikingly
pivots.why: Landing page builder side project took off, per YC Q&A.

outcome_analysis: Strikingly pivoted from a student crowdfunding idea to a simple mobile site builder, raised a $1.5M seed in 2013, then a $6M Series A in 2017 and a $10M round in 2018, reaching a stated total of about $17.5M. It competed with much larger builders but grew in China, reaching about 99 staff by the directory snapshot.
notes: The 2018 round is labelled Series A+ by TechCrunch and Series B by trackers; the CEO said it was technically Series B level, so stage is other. Series A investors conflict (CAS Holdings per Cathay Innovation snippet, Cathay per another); lead for 2018 is Cathay Capital. Founder education and employers not found. Strikingly launched 2012 or 2013 per conflicting sources. The YC Q&A says 320 employees while the directory says 99.
